--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.bfs_layers()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Group nodes by their hop distance from one or more sources. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.bfs_layers()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Group nodes by their hop distance from one or more sources. title: >- [Graph.bfs_layers()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Group nodes by their hop distance from one or more sources. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Group nodes by their hop distance from one or more sources. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L71628-L71742){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.bfs_layers( sources, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![BFS layers](../assets/graphs/bfs-layers.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="An eight-node graph searched from two sources at opposite ends, A and H. Each node is colored by its hop distance to the nearer source: A and H form layer 0 (accent), B, C, F, G layer 1 (teal), and D, E, where the two searches meet, layer 2 (violet). The card lists the three layers." width="100%"} Layer 0 holds the sources, layer 1 every node one hop away, layer 2 the nodes first reached at two hops, and so on: the rings a breadth-first search explores. With several sources, each node lands in the layer of its distance to the *nearest* source. Layers are useful for drawing a graph in concentric levels, for "friends of friends" style queries (layer 2), and as a fast, unweighted counterpart of `multi_source_shortest_path_length()`. Nodes that cannot be reached appear in no layer. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, list[Union[int, str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One starting node or a list of them, as integer IDs or string labels. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which way to follow edges on a directed graph: `"out"` (default), `"in"`, or `"all"`. Ignored for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The layers in order, each listing node IDs in discovery order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist or `mode=` is invalid. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~bfs`) : The order the search visits the nodes in. [](`~descendants_at_distance`) : The nodes at one distance only. [](`~multi_source_shortest_path_length`) : The distance to the nearest source, with weights. ## Examples {.doc-examples} From one end of a path, each layer holds one node; from both ends, the layers meet in the middle: ::: {#ff46b87e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(6) path.bfs_layers(1), path.bfs_layers([1, 6]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([[1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6]], [[1, 6], [2, 5], [3, 4]]) ``` ::: ::: ### Stops from the end of the line `metro()` is a made-up city's metro network. Starting from the stations at the ends of lines, those with a single neighbor, the layers count the stops from the nearest end: ::: {#c95b06e2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} metro = ec.metro() nodes = metro.get_node_df() ends = nodes.filter(nodes["degree"] == 1)["id"].to_list() layers = metro.bfs_layers(ends) [[metro.get_label_from_id(n) for n in layer] for layer in layers] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [['Docks', 'Shipyard', 'Airport'], ['Harbor', 'Business Park'], ['Riverside', 'Eastfield'], ['Central', 'Market', 'Old Town', 'Lakeside'], ['Museum', 'Opera', 'Mill Lane', 'Cathedral', 'Garden'], ['University', 'Westgate', 'Northpark'], ['Hillcrest']] ``` ::: ::: ### From the ends or from the center Each station colored by its layer. The only ends of lines are Docks, Shipyard and the Airport, so counted from them on the left, Hillcrest is six stops from the nearest end. Counted from Central on the right, no station is more than four stops away; the last layer holds the Airport, Garden and Hillcrest: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#c4124ef0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} def by_layer(layers): stops = {n: i for i, layer in enumerate(layers) for n in layer} return metro.set_node_attrs("stops", stops) by_layer(layers).plot( layout="pos", color_by="stops", color_scale="sequential", show_labels=False, width=320, height=320, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#c0b0840f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} by_layer(metro.bfs_layers("Central")).plot( layout="pos", color_by="stops", color_scale="sequential", show_labels=False, width=320, height=320, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
